title: Context-intelligence Unit E: bounded repository-intelligence views (census, cards, neighborhoods, question-oriented retrieval) (D-013)
objective: Bounded census views, file/symbol cards, dependency neighborhoods, and question-oriented retrieval feeding the ONE context compiler (never a second giant prompt); explicit coverage modes census/changed/neighborhood/deep with full machine-readable coverage records and provenance.
business_reason: D-013 Unit E; retrieval views over the deterministic index.
inputs: tools/repo_index_incremental.py build_incremental (accepted A1/A2 index + telemetry: census, change_set, versions, fingerprints — consumed read-only in process)
tools/subsystem_resolver.py + tools/subsystem_entities.py (accepted Unit C versioned ontology — read-only)
tools/memory_graph.py memory_store (accepted Unit D external store — read-only, advisory)
D-013 requirements R023 (coverage modes), R024 (coverage-record minimum fields), R039/R042 (feed the ONE compiler, no filling), R009/R018 (deterministic, honest kinds), R013 (fail closed)
outputs: tools/repo_views.py — core bounded view builders: census view (every eligible file accounted indexed/excluded/failed with reasons), changed view (this run's deterministic change classification vs the prior cache generation, fail-closed on unsupported base fingerprints), dependency neighborhood view, file/symbol card view (kind, subsystem via Unit C, bounded edges), deep view (exact bounded source excerpt with digest + line provenance), plus the R024 coverage-record builder with a separate labeled non-identity cache-state section

tools/repo_views_query.py — deterministic question-oriented retrieval (about_file/about_task/about_requirement/who_imports/what_changed) returning bounded structured answers with coverage records and machine-readable no-answers; bounded CLI (census/changed/card/neighborhood/deep/ask/check with a determinism self-proof)
tools/test_repo_views.py — executable AS-1..AS-6 acceptance tests + truncation, no-answer, fail-closed and cold-vs-warm determinism cases
docs/REPO_VIEWS.md — the views contract: modes, coverage-record fields, bounds/truncation semantics, advisory memory reads, Unit B/compiler consumption notes

acceptance_scenarios.given: the deterministic index over a fixture repository
acceptance_scenarios.then: every view labels its coverage_mode from exactly {census, changed, neighborhood, deep}; the census view accounts for EVERY eligible file as indexed or excluded/failed with per-reason groups (census.reconciles true); the changed view reports this run's deterministic change classification (added/content_modified/metadata_modified/deleted/renamed + global invalidators) against the prior cache generation and REFUSES an unsupported stated base fingerprint; the neighborhood view is bounded around a named seed; the deep view returns an exact bounded excerpt with content digest and line provenance (D-013-R023)

it machine-readably carries repository identity, snapshot fingerprint, HEAD/branch/dirty-state digest, eligible/indexed counts, excluded and failed files grouped by reason, stale count, indexer/schema/config versions PLUS the Unit C ontology version stamp, source manifest digest, export digest, and the EXACT query parameters and result limits; cache hit/miss and rebuild fields live in a separate section explicitly labeled non-identity cache state (D-013-R024)

acceptance_scenarios.given: a query whose full result exceeds the view's limit
acceptance_scenarios.then: output is truncated at the recorded limit WITH a machine-readable truncation marker (count of omitted items) — never silently; views return bounded structured data for the ONE compiler and never assemble a prompt, budget, or capacity-filling content of their own (D-013-R039/R042/R003)

all retrieval is deterministic code (no LLM anywhere); reported node/edge kinds are exactly those in the index export; subsystem labels come ONLY from the versioned Unit C resolver; an unresolvable seed/question returns a machine-readable no-answer (never a guess); memory-graph reads are labeled advisory and an absent/empty store is labeled, never fabricated (D-013-R009/R018/R045/R051)

acceptance_scenarios.given: an unavailable/corrupt index, a non-canonical or out-of-tree deep-view path, and an unreadable task packet
acceptance_scenarios.then: each refuses with a machine-readable error (CLI exit 2) — index_unavailable / non_canonical_path / path_not_in_tree / task_packet_unreadable; no partial answer is ever presented as complete (D-013-R013)

acceptance_scenarios.given: identical repository state and arguments, cold cache then warm cache
acceptance_scenarios.when: the same view is built in both runs
acceptance_scenarios.then: the deterministic sections (view content + coverage record) are byte-identical across cold and warm; only the labeled non-identity cache-state section may differ; the CLI check subcommand self-proves this (D-013-R037-style determinism)

risks: Coverage-record drift: R024 names many required fields; mitigated by a single coverage-record builder used by every view + AS-2 field assertions
Scope creep into Unit F: no benchmarks/runbook and no initiative status projection here; this unit is retrieval views only
path_free_justification: Paths bound at claim (2026-08-18) after M0-T067 acceptance, per the D-013 sequencing reservation (source-002). New bounded-views modules consuming the accepted A1/A2 index, Unit C resolver, and Unit D store strictly read-only; no existing module is rewritten.
